name: Sog
prior: Riser+impact tools all trigger the impact by time or by a second note, never by note-off scaled by hold time: AIR The Riser (synth; sweep length follows note pitch/host tempo, a riser can be reversed into a crash; VS: djworx.com/?p=16003, djworx review-riser-synth-air-music-technology), NI Rise & Hit (sample layers rise/hit, latch plays the whole sample regardless of key hold; VS: sonicstate 2014/04/16, kvraudio forum t=440055 - 'impact toggle only works in manual mode, not via MIDI'), Whoosh/Gravity-type builders (VS: kvraudio t=440055, integraudio 8-best-sweep-riser-plugins), Krotos synth-riser presets (VS: krotos.studio). Release-stage patches exist as a concept ('a NOTE_OFF message does not mean end of note ... patches which trigger a pitch sweep at Release', Dobson 1999; VS: sound.media.mit.edu saol-dev/1999/0176) and Serum/Vital/Phase Plant expose note-off as a modulation source (A), but no instrument found in two searches (one extended) where the hit is fired by the release and its weight is the hold time. Myzel: Brandung (composer) is a Duffing breaker, Tiefe a tanh growl; nothing inverts the envelope. The DSP itself (bandpassed noise sweep, tremolo tone, sine drop + splash) is stock trailer vocabulary - the novelty is 100 % in the gesture, which is why 'new' is a gesture rating, not a timbre rating.
costNotes: Native, two phases that barely overlap: build-up = noise buffer + BQ bandpass + 3 oscillators (PeriodicWave at f, tremolo LFO, sub) + ~4 gains ~ 9 nodes ~ 0.4-0.5 units (oscillators and biquads sit at the 0.06 end, gains at 0.03; R: webaudio.md section 4); breaker = 1 sine + 2 noise sources + HP + LP + 3 gains ~ 0.3 for 1-4 s. Time-averaged ~0.55-0.6 as the idea says; L3 (stereo splash, second osc, 2x shaper on the sub with oversample 'none') ~1.1. All automation is setTargetAtTime/ramps on native params, Bebung through v.mod on detune, no worklet. One PeriodicWave 'sog' cached in A.waves (APP 2809). Cheap; the cost is not the problem.
soundHeld: A held note is a crescendo, not a tone: bandpassed noise rising 2f -> 16f over Dauer, a 1/n-spectrum tone at f with a tremolo that accelerates 5 -> 11 Hz, a sub creeping in late. Pitch identity is weak in the build (noise dominates once the bandpass leaves the note) and strong only in the hit (2.5f -> f sine drop = an 808-style boom at fold(f)). Two structural problems: (1) after Dauer the voice is at full tension with nowhere to go - a long ambient hold becomes a static shimmer waiting for a crash, and every release crashes, so Sog cannot play a quiet phrase; k (release speed) scales only Schaum, so a slow lift still booms. A 'Brecher' parameter down to 0 (or H below a threshold = foam only) is needed for ambient use. (2) The gesture contradicts the Spielhilfe ('loslassen = ausklingen'), sustain pedal and Gestik Tragen: with the pedal every held note crashes at pedal-up, together - fun once, chaos in a chord. Tremolo (5-11 Hz) and Bebung (vibrato on the detune bus) collide on the same note. Loudness: Wucht*H*vel plus splash can sit 6-10 dB above the build; needs a per-engine reference level like Tiefe's. With three fingers released in sequence it is genuinely a set of breaking waves - the one musical image no other engine gives.
soundBurst: In Puls every sustaining engine gets gate 0.22 s via hit() (APP 5083), so H = clamp(0.22/3, 0.15, 1) = 0.15: every hit is the minimum breaker, a 200 ms whoosh and a small boom landing ~200 ms AFTER the step. The idea's 'Brecher auf die Eins' only works if the engine starts the build before the scheduled time (Puls stamps pulses ahead, APP 8208, so a negative offset is possible but is new scheduler plumbing) or if the burst is simply inverted: boom at t, foam after. At 1/16 it is a whoosh machine with identical hits; decayMul only scales Schaum. As a lane engine it needs its own burst design (hit first, build optional), not the held design run short.
failureModes: Every release booms: no quiet phrasing, no ambient use; needs a Brecher/Wucht floor of 0 and H<0.15 = foam only.
Puls hit lands at gate end (+0.2 s), not on the step; grid-locked playing needs a pre-start offset or an inverted burst (hit first).
Sustain pedal / Tragen defer the release: all notes crash at once on pedal-up.
Weak pitch identity while held (noise sweep dominates after ~1 s); only the hit says the note.
Tremolo 5-11 Hz vs Bebung vibrato on the same voice = beating mess; tremolo must duck when Bebung is active.
Loudness jump build -> hit (6-10 dB); needs a calibrated reference and a ceiling on Wucht*H*vel.
Stock trailer-FX timbre (riser + boom + splash): without the natural-world dressing (foam = lowpass noise, not white) it reads as a free SFX pack.
Stolen voice in the build loses the breaker (acceptable, as the idea says).
verdict: New as a gesture - no instrument found where the impact is fired by note-off and weighted by how long you held - but the sounds themselves (noise riser, tremolo tone, sine drop, splash) are the most common cinematic vocabulary there is, so the engine lives or dies on the gesture, not the timbre. Native and cheap (~0.6 / 1.1). As a held note it is a crescendo that must crash, which contradicts Myzel's release convention, the sustain pedal and ambient play; as a Puls hit the breaker lands 200 ms late and every hit is the minimum H. Keep it only with a Brecher floor of 0 (quiet lifts = foam), a hit-first burst variant for Puls, and tremolo ducking under Bebung; otherwise it is a one-trick trailer button.
